entry.title: [Kayhan_online] Kayhan investigates 🔰 Securing gas for the northern provinces is one of the…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Kayhan_online

Kayhan investigates 🔰 Securing gas for the northern provinces is one of the president's goals on his trip to Turkmenistan

🔸With the onset of the cold season, the gas imbalance will become apparent, especially in the north of the country; therefore, the president, who is heading to Turkmenistan today, must pursue the import and swap of gas from the northern neighbor.

🔸According to our reporter, our country, due to its vast geography and the unparalleled coverage of the household gas network, along with the dependence of power plants and various industries on gas fuel, has faced an imbalance between production and consumption. The enemy's attack on South Pars during the 40-day war, although it met with Iran's decisive and unexpected response to the gas facilities of "Ras Laffan" and caught the enemy off guard, part of the country's gas production was also damaged and the imbalances worsened.

🔸Damage to five phases of the South Pars refineries during the Ramadan war reduced the country's daily gas production capacity by about 230 million cubic meters. So far, according to the National Gas Company, 95 million cubic meters of gas have returned to the grid, and currently there is a deficit of 135 million cubic meters of gas.

🔸If the upcoming winter is similar to last year's winter in terms of temperature and consumption, and only 95 million cubic meters of the damaged capacity is restored, the gas deficit will be about 130 million cubic meters, which, combined with the previous imbalance figure, will total about 380 million cubic meters per day.

🔸The gas shortage problem is not limited to homes, and power plants, in order to prevent power outages for household subscribers, are forced to turn to alternative fuels, namely diesel and fuel oil. The increased consumption of fuel oil, or mazut, also leads to an increase in pollutants and worsening air pollution.

🔸Of course, gas imports from Turkmenistan also face obstacles. The story of gas imports from this country began with a 25-year contract concluded between the parties in 1997, but due to financial problems that arose during Bijan Zangeneh's ministry in Hassan Rouhani's government, it ran into trouble in subsequent years. Of course, the other side also had breaches of commitment, which ultimately, with the weak defense of the Iranian side in the legal dispute, resulted in our country being fined. This fine and its consequences have cast a shadow over oil transfers between the two countries in recent years.

🔸Despite all these problems, during the era of the martyred Raisi in the Thirteenth Government and with Iran's personal follow-up, Iran was able to receive the right of oil swap between Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan in the form of gas. Now the Fourteenth Government must exert all its power to renew this matter — whether in the form of swap rights or direct import.

With the announcement of the withdrawal of American military forces from Iraq, should the Popular Mobilization Forces (Hashd al-Shaabi) be dissolved? For various reasons, the answer is no. First, although American military forces have been forced to evacuate their bases as a result of attacks by Iran and the Axis of Resistance, the anti-security American embassy is still active in Iraq with more than seven thousand personnel and several thousand contractors under various cover. These very illegal pressures of the American occupiers are definitive proof that resistance and popular mobilization must continue as the main pillar of pushing back American threats and pressures. Whenever those pressures are completely eliminated, one of the requirements for the formation of the Hashd al-Shaabi will also cease to exist. Second, another important function of the Iraqi Popular Mobilization Forces has been effective resistance and struggle against proxy terrorist groups such as ISIS and remnants of the Baath Party. Although ISIS has been largely suppressed, numerous pieces of evidence indicate America's and some other regimes' efforts to revive ISIS with newer and more updated versions. Syria, in the vicinity of Iraq, had previously witnessed the reorganization of the terrorist group Tahrir al-Sham by Turkey and America. Infiltration, negligence, and the debilitation of the army caused the fall of that country at the hands of these proxy mercenaries of America. Syria is now experiencing a state of disintegration, insecurity, the destruction of its defense infrastructure by the Zionists, and a severe economic crisis. entry.title: [Kayhan_online] #Virtual_Space_Roaming🔰Let's read the table so we don't become a mere…

Source: @Kayhan_online

#Virtual_Space_Roaming🔰Let's read the table so we don't become a mere shopfront🔺Maybe the development model is something other than buying Ronaldo!🔸Iran's young caravan — a nation that has been through war — in days when even coming and going through the skies was difficult for it, reached sixth place in Asia with 19 golds, 18 silvers, and 15 bronzes;◽It became the best country in West Asia by a wide margin◾It reeled in 6 more gold medals than the previous edition of the competitions◽Its girls claimed a 15-medal share of the caravan's 52 medals◾And it was only 3 more golds away from achieving the best result in its history...Hats off to them and may they stay in good health.🔸Saudi Arabia, too, reached twentieth place in the table with 3 golds, 2 silvers, and 9 bronzes — above Singapore and below Vietnam; it maintained the gap it has always had with Iran, and likely, with the rise of Iranian female athletes in recent years, that gap will only widen.🔸Of course, I have always avoided/avoid this kind of induction, but since for several years the most inefficient and backward development model — one that views every manifestation of development as a mere shopfront — has been used to humiliate Iranians, I say: Perhaps the "development model" should be something other than buying foreign players at ten times their market price for a seductive show in the domestic league... It is where the Portuguese Ronaldo cannot take the field in place of a Saudi athlete and win a medal that the true measure of nations' progress finally becomes clear... Just as in wartime, the true measure of a cheap military force — one whose software, hardware, and infantry arise from its own soil, science, and national awareness — is revealed against the world's greatest military power; and the impurity of an expensive army becomes apparent when, after being branded a "milking cow" and buying up countless fighter jets and Patriot systems and hiring hundreds of thousands of mercenaries from other countries, they are ultimately deployed to fight against a besieged land with the least possible military logistics — and get stuck in the mud.🔸Which problem does sports solve? To be honest, none! It was never supposed to solve any particular problem from the start, but it is a good mirror for reflecting a society's perception... If on the day our club team, worth about 15 million dollars, loses to a Saudi club team worth about 200 million dollars, we feel backwardness and humiliation — but when in a global event the gap between Iranian and Saudi national players reveals itself to this degree and we do not look at it "differently," it means that before anything else, we have lost the capacity for independent thinking — we too have become a shopfront!💬 Mohammad Sadegh Faramarzi🔘 Yes | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram@Kayhan_Online

🔰The Special Place of Minab's Children at the 38th Children's Film Festival
🔸The 38th Children and Adolescents Film Festival, taking place in Isfahan from 11 to 16 Mehr, will give special attention to the martyrs and the children of Minab.
🔸According to a Kayhan reporter, Hamed Jafari, CEO of the Farabi Cinema Foundation and secretary of the 38th Children and Adolescents Film Festival, stated at the event's press conference: Contrary to expectations of a possible drop in participation due to the aftermath of the recent war, which had disrupted production, filmmakers' turnout for this edition has fortunately been unprecedented, with registrations nearly double those of previous editions. Regarding this edition's special focus on the second and third imposed wars and the children of Minab, he explained: Out of respect for the martyred children of Minab, all of the festival's usual special sections have been eliminated, and only the special Minab section and award will be held. A dedicated poster and statuette have been designed for this section. Additionally, in the Minab screenwriting competition, which drew widespread participation, 4 top proposals were selected from among 423 submissions and their screenplays were completed, with the winners to be announced during the festival.
🔸The secretary of the 38th Children and Adolescents Film Festival continued, noting structural changes and the addition of new sections to the event, and added: In order to recognize the efforts of the technical crew in children's cinema, who are less visible at festivals, awards have been added for technical categories such as acting, editing, and music. New sections have also been added to this edition, including artificial intelligence, to address emerging technologies; a documentary section in workshop format; and the Mirror section, aimed at reviewing and analyzing works broadcast on platforms and television, with a focus on audience engagement and product development.
🔸He added: The Adolescents Filmmaking Olympiad, which was halted last year due to special circumstances, will also be held this year alongside the festival in Isfahan.
🔸Jafari announced the names of the 15 feature-length fiction films selected for the competition section of this edition of the Children's Festival as follows: Badbadak-ha, Pelk-e Parishan-e Parvaneh, Do Tofangdar, Shootinga, Arous-e Cheshmeh, Amu-ye Bacheh-ha, Kakaluti, Kuch, Gorgi Khan, Man Jasouzan Nistam, Nabegheh va Div-e Sangi, Negahbanan-e Khorshid, Noor, Varkana, and Yeki Miad Donbalam. #Adab_va_Honar🔘 Bale | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram@Kayhan_Online

🔸The letter of His Eminence Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader of the Revolution, to his brother Ayatollah Sayyid Mostafa Khamenei during his adolescence and during his presence on the frontlines of the Sacred Defense has been published:

🔺In His Exalted Name

🔰The missing arrow in the bow of sports management!🔸Gholamreza Shabani-Bahar, head of the Archery Federation, went on Radio Varzesh yesterday after the recurve competitions at the 2026 Asian Games to discuss the problems and costs of this discipline—a discipline that is equipment-driven and involves specialized gear with specific, calculable costs.🔸But what stood out more than archery's problems in this roughly 10-minute conversation was the bizarre muddle in stating the simplest numbers and figures. When the talk turned to the price of an arrow, the numbers kept changing one after another: first 12 million tomans, then 120 million tomans, then one billion and 200 million tomans, and finally back to 120 million tomans again! A listener who was supposed to learn about the financial problems of a sports discipline probably ended the conversation not so much understanding how much archery costs, but rather wondering: what on earth is going on in sports?!🔸The issue here is not merely a slip of the tongue or a misplaced zero. When the head of a federation—in a discipline where he has been involved for years—cannot give a clear and precise figure for one of the most basic and fundamental costs of the discipline he manages, one has to ask: what has happened to sports management?!🔸It is only natural that the price of specialized equipment varies depending on brand, quality, country of origin, and the athlete's level, and no one expects a federation head to have memorized the price list for every equipment model. But the expectation is that when he speaks with the national media about his discipline's problems, he should at least have a clear, precise, and reliable picture of its main costs.🔸At least once, we need to seriously ask: what has happened to sports that a federation head, in a media interview about one of the most basic issues of the discipline he manages, cannot provide a specific and reliable figure?🔸Of course, the problem is not just Shabani-Bahar; the problem is a structure in which sports managers sometimes have no grasp of the issues in their own discipline—and unfortunately, their number is not small!#نکته_ورزشی #سرویس_ورزشی🔘 بله | ایتا | سروش+ | اینستاگرام | تلگرام@Kayhan_Online

Deterrent Defense Shield: Negotiation or Counter-Offensive? - 2

After several rounds of failed military operations and the humiliation that followed, the enemy's guard shifted to economic siege and hostility. But unfortunately, some managers, advisers, and analysts still deal with it through the negotiation guard (the catalyst of the enemy's plot).

Certainly, military threats must not be neglected or underestimated. But neither should the enemy's intensified helplessness be forgotten, nor should it be given excessive weight, breeding passivity and fear, and causing neglect of a decisive response to the economic war and siege.

Concern about the enemy's military threat and "treating negotiation as a shelter," even if it had been correct — which it was not — belonged to the stage before the enemy's repeated betrayal of negotiations and imposition of war.

When the war happened, the illusion that negotiation and agreement serve as a deterrent defense shield collapsed. Therefore, one must not again create a bubble for oneself and others and retreat into a shell of passivity; for this behavior amounts to being played by the worn-out tactic of the madman.

The economic siege (maritime and aerial), backed by military action, is a one hundred percent aggressive and criminal military action that must be answered by deploying all kinds of military and non-military threats, symmetrical and asymmetrical.

The enemy has targeted your economy; you too must forcefully strike at its economic interests and Achilles' heels in the commercial and energy domains, the infrastructure related to undersea cables, and... in the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandab, the Indian Ocean, the Sea of Oman, and the Persian Gulf.

This necessary action is precisely the opposite of passive negotiation-seeking, of pressuring the military forces not to bare their claws at America's criminal partners in the region (the UAE and...), and of calming the energy market.

All polls indicate the free fall of Trump's popularity and its clear damage to the position of his political supporters in next month's congressional elections.

The pressure must not be lifted from America. In this regard, the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council has adopted intelligent and powerful positions, and it is expected that this position will not be weakened by one-sided negotiation signals.

Also, the hands of the operating forces on the ground must be opened wider, and no restrictions or constraints should be created for them.

Not the slightest notion should take shape in the enemy's mind that, in the Iranian side's view, field-oriented actions have subsided and the emphasis and reliance is only on negotiation. This notion is inherently anti-authority and even undermines bargaining power should negotiation become necessary.

Deterrent Defense Shield: Negotiation or Counter-Offensive? – 1

When your opponent in a contest—a fight—changes stance, you too must change your stance and not remain passive.

America and Israel had clearly come up short in the forty-day war, and the tide had turned, prompting them to seek a ceasefire through intermediaries:

- National unity and cohesion, contrary to the plan for the January overthrow and coup, had been revived and reached its peak.
- The Strait of Hormuz had been closed, humiliating America.
- A significant portion of their offensive and defensive munitions had run out or been strategically depleted.
- Key American bases in the region had been struck. They had nearly been rendered inoperable, yet were still imposing considerable costs on the Pentagon.
- Dozens of fighter jets, helicopters, and drones had been shot down.
- Attempts to reopen the strait or penetrate deep into Iran had failed.
- Iran kept revealing new intelligence and military cards.
- Oil prices during the war had risen to $126.
- And more...

One can accept that, for certain considerations, the Iranian side agreed to a (temporary) ceasefire and would use this time to regroup and reorganize forces, capabilities, and plans.

What is not reasonable was tying the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to the ceasefire.

There was no reason that, while the hostile party had twice betrayed during negotiations and committed great and unprecedented crimes, it should receive a concession on the level of reopening the strait through that strange tweet by Mr. Araghchi.

What was America's reaction? Trump, at the same time as oil prices crashed, announced he would impose a naval blockade against Iran!

This, even though at the height of the war, under pressure from oil prices, he had been forced to suspend some oil sanctions so that Iranian oil could reach the market.

If the justification is an existential threat, Trump later raised this threat more than ten more times. And before that, he never shied away from any crime—unless he was unable to commit it.

Delving into the rest of the story regarding the "memorandum of understanding" is beyond the scope of this analysis.

Whatever judgment we hold about the memorandum of understanding—whether we call it an "honor—a great achievement" or deem it a "mirage/deception operation"—unfortunately, the stance of some of those in charge has not changed after the enemy violated the agreement.

💢To be continued

🔰Wandering in Cyberspace🔸A highly valuable insight into the character of the Supreme Leader of the Revolution🔸A very interesting point that became clearly evident from the first message of the new Leader of the Revolution, and is both highly valuable and rare, is that he is extremely attentive to details and also very insistent that even seemingly insignificant details be conveyed to the people with complete honesty.🔸How was the clenched fist—which has now become a symbol of resistance—first brought up?🔸In one part of the message, he said: "I had this blessing to visit his body after his martyrdom; what I saw was a mountain of steadfastness; and I heard that he had clenched the fist of his healthy hand."🔸In these same three simple sentences, interesting details have been presented. He has stated that he himself saw the body of the martyred Leader, but he himself did not see his clenched fist at that moment, and others later told him that he had clenched the fist of his healthy hand! Whereas he could have easily glossed over these details and said that he saw the body of the martyred Leader and that his fist was clenched.🔸The matter of honestly declaring "I originally had a different opinion" is another clear example of this aspect of his character, which needs no further explanation.🔸In his condolence message for the passing of Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani, various such subtleties can be seen, one of which is this sentence: "This honorable scholar spent his entire noble life—except for the first few years of childhood—on the path of learning and teaching and research"🔸When it is said that a person spent his life on the path of learning and teaching, it does not mean the period of his childhood, but the Supreme Leader of the Revolution does not simply pass over this seemingly obvious matter either, and writes his words with precision and exact details, and specifies that the matter of him having spent his life on this path does not include the first few years of childhood!🔸All this precision and honesty in expression at the highest position of the country is very valuable and, God willing, heralds a much better future.Mohammadreza Nazari🔘 Yes | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram@Kayhan_Online
